Understand customers and members

Users is your customer list. A user on that page is a customer record, not a teammate with a JOHN CRM login. The people who work in your CRM are members, managed in Workspace → Members.

Website visitors

Website visitors stay in External Chat until you choose Create client. Promoting a visitor makes the record visible in Users and moves the conversation to Internal Chat.

Create and maintain a customer record

  1. 1Open Users and choose Add New User. Enter the full name, then add useful contact details. Include the country code for WhatsApp numbers.
  2. 2Choose applicable User Types and complete their fields. Add relevant, current notes to User Memory, then save the record.
  3. 3Use search or User Type filters to find the customer again. Open the record to review details and use Edit when information changes.

Keep stored answers and their headings intact when editing User Memory. Notes help your team and AI understand the customer; editing a note does not grant messaging consent or change a customer’s opt-out.

Organise customers with User Types

Manage User Types from Configurations → User Type, or the User types button on Users if your role allows it. Create a meaningful type, such as Member or Student, and define any fields it needs. Apply it in a customer’s record.

  • User Types support customer filtering and audiences. They can also grant access to restricted Knowledge Base spaces, so review that effect before changing a customer’s types.
  • Local fields are stored in JOHN CRM. API-backed types connect to another system; check the save result if the external source is unavailable or only partly updated.

Invite your team

  1. 1As an owner or administrator with invitation permission, open Workspace → Members → Invite member.
  2. 2Enter the teammate’s email and choose the appropriate role. Send the invitation; pending invitations reserve workspace seats.
  3. 3Ask them to open the invitation using that email and accept it. Use Workspace → Invites to check pending invitations, resend a link or revoke one.

Standard workspace invitations expire after seven days. If the seat limit is reached, review unused invitations and available seats before inviting again.

Review roles and permissions

A member’s base role and any custom roles determine their access. Workspace → Workspace Roles shows the available roles. Owners and administrators can manage roles within their own permission limits; some built-in roles are protected.

Open a member’s editor and Manage access to inspect effective permissions and the roles granting them. You cannot use role editing to raise someone above your own level or change your own access. Removing a member takes away access immediately and unassigns their customers; shared knowledge stays in the workspace.

Someone cannot see or change a feature

Confirm their email, accepted membership and selected workspace. Then inspect their effective permissions rather than relying only on the role name: workspaces can customise some roles. Ask an owner or administrator to grant the necessary access. If the whole feature is unavailable, ask John Support about the workspace’s enabled features.
